name: com.mygamedevtools.fixed-input
description:
A deterministic fixed-step tick and a one-shot input intent bound to a single step.

An intent is valid for exactly one fixed simulation step and expires by arithmetic. Nothing clears it, nothing consumes it twice, and a paused or reloaded game cannot deliver a stale press:

┃ if (input.Attack.TryConsume(tick))
┃     Attack();

The point is the input surface between them. A device writer and a scripted agent fill the same struct, and whatever reads it cannot tell which one is live, so every mechanic written for a player works for an agent the day it ships.

▪ A tick source that installs into the PlayerLoop, needing no scene object and no script execution order.
▪ Per-read buffering windows, so one press can be frame-exact for one reader and lenient for another.
▪ A peek/consume split, so a condition that merely tests an intent cannot eat it.
▪ Development-build diagnostics that name an intent nobody consumed, instead of a character that mysteriously ignores input.
▪ Optional Entities support, compiled only when the Entities package is present.

samples.description: One character driven by a device and by a scripted agent through the same input surface, movement included. A runtime toggle swaps the writer and the reader never notices.
The same demonstration in ECS: one reader system, a device writer and an agent writer, all through one IComponentData input surface. Requires the Entities package.
